poem:
## The Sprue-Tree

'Twas brillig, and the waxen sprue
Did gimbal down the molten chute;
All mimsy were the sprong-blobs too,
And the mould-core, a-hoot.

"Beware the Sprue-Tree, oh my son!
The branches hot, the channels deep!
Beware the cast-out, every one,
And shun the flow-hole's weep!"

He took his vorpal mould in hand;
Long time the Sprue-Tree foe he sought—
So rested he by the drag-draw stand,
And stood awhile in thought.

And, as in uffish thought he stood,
The Sprue-Tree, with its sprong-blob cast,
Came whiffling through the green-sand wood,
And burbled as it passed!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
His vorpal mould went snicker-snack!
He left it dead, and with its crew
He went a-cooling back.

"And hast thou slain the Sprue-Tree foe?
Bring forth the casting, bright and boon!
O frabjous day! Calooh! Callow!"
He chortled in his joy-moon.

'Twas brillig, and the waxen sprue
Did gimbal down the molten chute;
All mimsy were the sprong-blobs too,
And the mould-core, a-hoot.
